items.prompt: Explain the distinction between wage and non-wage factors in choosing an occupation.
items.canonical_answer: Wage factors concern monetary remuneration; non-wage factors concern features such as hours, conditions, security or development rather than the immediate money wage.
marking_guidance: Difference (1): monetary remuneration. Contrast/test (1): job characteristics distinct from immediate pay.

items.prompt: Explain why a worker might choose a lower-paid offer with a shorter journey when both offers meet essential income needs and caring time is the priority.
items.canonical_answer: The shorter journey releases time for caring, a valued non-wage benefit. With essential income already met, that benefit can outweigh the extra pay forgone.
marking_guidance: Context (1): priority for caring and shorter journey. Reason/conclusion (1): non-wage time benefit outweighs additional pay under the supplied constraint.

items.prompt: Explain the difference between basic pay and journey time as factors in an occupational choice.
items.canonical_answer: Basic pay is monetary remuneration, a wage factor. Journey time is a non-wage characteristic affecting the time cost and convenience of the job.
marking_guidance: Difference (1): basic pay is monetary. Contrast (1): journey time is a non-wage characteristic.

items.prompt: Explain the monetary comparison using invented monthly offers with other deductions ignored: A pays N$8,000 with N$800 travel cost; B pays N$7,200 with N$200 travel cost.
items.canonical_answer: After the stated travel expenditure, A leaves N$7,200 and B N$7,000. A’s financial advantage is N$200 on this measure, not the N$800 difference in headline pay.
marking_guidance: Context (1): account for stated travel costs. Reason/conclusion (1): compare N$7,200 versus N$7,000, a N$200 advantage.

items.prompt: Explain the distinction between training opportunities and an overtime payment in an occupational choice.
items.canonical_answer: Training is a development characteristic, a non-wage feature. The overtime payment is monetary remuneration for stated work, a wage factor.
marking_guidance: Difference (1): training/development feature. Contrast (1): overtime money is remuneration.

items.prompt: Explain one non-wage reason to prefer a job offering relevant training when immediate pay is sufficient but developing a skill is the individual’s priority.
items.canonical_answer: Relevant training supports the stated development goal, so it can make the job more attractive without requiring a higher immediate wage; later promotion is not guaranteed.
marking_guidance: Context (1): relevant training matches development priority. Reason/consequence (1): non-wage development benefit supports choice, without guaranteeing promotion.

items.prompt: Identify two wage factors in occupational choice (2). Identify two non-wage factors (2). Explain why safer working conditions can affect a supplied choice where safety is the worker’s priority and pay is adequate (2). Identify a wage and a non-wage feature from this invented offer: monthly basic pay and relevant training (2).
items.canonical_answer: Basic pay and an overtime payment are wage factors. Journey time and safety conditions are non-wage factors. Safer conditions address the worker’s stated priority and can outweigh additional pay if adequate income is available. The offer’s basic pay is wage-related and training non-wage development.
marking_guidance: Identification, separate points (2): basic pay (1), overtime pay (1). Non-wage points (2): journey time (1), safety (1). Explanation (2): safer conditions match priority (1), can determine choice when pay is adequate (1). Final features (2): basic pay wage (1), training non-wage (1). Marks allocation 8.

items.prompt: Invented Namibian monthly offers, with other deductions ignored: A pays N$8,000, travel costs N$800 and total daily travel takes two hours; B pays N$7,200, travel costs N$200 and travel takes half an hour. Working hours are otherwise the same. B offers relevant training. Describe three differences relevant to the choice (6). Explain how money remaining after travel and non-wage features can change the headline-pay comparison (7). Discuss which offer suits someone prioritising caring time and skill development, with essential income needs met by either offer (7).
items.canonical_answer: A pays more, has greater travel cost and requires a longer journey; B also offers training. After stated travel expenditure A leaves N$7,200 and B N$7,000, narrowing the monetary difference to N$200. B saves one and a half hours each working day and offers a relevant development opportunity, without guaranteed promotion. B better serves the stated caring/development priorities if its pay remains adequate and training is useful. A retains a financial advantage, so a change in urgent income needs could alter the conclusion.
marking_guidance: Context/data description (6): pay difference (1), N$8,000/N$7,200 evidence (1); travel cost difference (1), N$800/N$200 evidence (1); travel time difference (1), two hours/half-hour evidence (1). Mechanism/explanation (7): A remaining N$7,200 (1), B remaining N$7,000 (1), gap only N$200 (1); B saves 1.5 hours (1), supporting caring (1); training supports development (1), not guaranteed promotion (1). Both sides/judgement (7): A offers extra money (1), may help income needs (1); B offers time (1), development (1); condition adequate income/useful training (1); choose B for stated priority (1), reconsider if financial constraint changes (1). Marks allocation 6+7+7=20.

facts: Invented Namibian monthly offers, with other deductions ignored: A pays N$8,000, travel costs N$800 and total daily travel takes two hours; B pays N$7,200, travel costs N$200 and travel takes half an hour. Working hours are otherwise the same. B offers relevant training.

items.prompt: Invented Namibian monthly offers, with other deductions ignored: A pays N$8,000, travel costs N$800 and total daily travel takes two hours; B pays N$7,200, travel costs N$200 and travel takes half an hour. Working hours are otherwise the same. B offers relevant training. Evaluate the choice in two seven-mark plans. Case 1: an individual urgently values the extra money and can manage the longer journey. Case 2: either offer meets essential income needs, while caring time and useful training are decisive. Include opposing arguments and the condition supporting each judgement.
items.canonical_answer: Case 1: A’s N$200 extra after the stated travel cost supports the urgent income priority, but longer travel sacrifices time and B’s training is forgone. Choose A if the extra income matters more and travel is manageable. Case 2: B saves 1.5 daily hours and offers training, but gives up N$200 on the stated measure. Choose B if income remains adequate and training is relevant; no guaranteed future promotion should be assumed.
marking_guidance: Case 1 marks (7): argument for more remaining income (1), meets urgent need (1); argument against longer travel (1), forgone development (1); condition manageable journey and stronger income priority (1); judgement A (1) tied to that condition (1). Case 2 allocation (7): argument for time saving (1), relevant training (1); argument against less remaining income (1), development outcome uncertain (1); condition adequate income and useful training (1); judgement B (1) tied to the stated priorities (1). Total 14.
